summary: The article offers strategies for parents of picky eaters, built around making healthy food fun, involving kids in preparation, and teaching them about food. It draws on quotes and events from experts, including a dietician, a chef, a teacher, a child psychologist, a pediatrician and a speech-language pathologist. It closes with a Super Smoothie Bowl recipe and tips on presentation, texture, snacks and conversation.
one_line: A guide to getting picky eaters to enjoy healthy food through creativity, involvement, education, routine, portion control, and a Super Smoothie Bowl recipe.
key_facts: A study in the "Journal of Pediatric Psychology" published September 5, 2023 found nearly 50% of parents identify their preschoolers as picky eaters.
Registered dietician Jessica Torres, a mother of two, says handling picky eaters is about balance: introduce new flavors in familiar settings.
Chef and father Michael Davidson said on October 12, 2023 at a family cooking workshop, "If they help make it, they're more likely to try it."
Parenting blogger Sarah Johnson wrote on September 15, 2023 that her children are far more eager to eat food they helped prepare.
Teacher Maria Gonzales started a "Garden to Table" program at her school on September 22, 2023, saying children who know where food comes from are more likely to try new things.
Child psychologist Diane Matthews advises that a regular eating routine helps children feel secure, and suggests Taco Tuesday with a new vegetable each week.
Pediatrician Dr. Oliver Thompson said on November 3, 2023 that large portions can overwhelm children and lead them to reject a meal before trying it.
The Super Smoothie Bowl was created with input from Sarah Johnson and Jessica Torres and uses 1 frozen banana, ½ cup frozen berries, ½ cup spinach and ¾ cup milk of choice.
The smoothie bowl has optional 1 tablespoon honey and toppings such as granola, sliced fruits, nuts, seeds or yogurt; all base ingredients are blended until smooth and kids decorate it.
A food art workshop for parents on November 20, 2023 highlighted that eye-catching meal presentation increases a child's willingness to eat.
Speech-language pathologist Elizabeth Harris recommended on December 1, 2023 introducing textures slowly, emphasizing creamy, crunchy and chewy foods.
Healthier snack ideas include energy balls made with oats and fruit puree and baked veggie chips.
